headline: Paperclip Turns AI Agents Into a Workforce
lede: Paperclip gives autonomous agents an organization chart, budgets, permissions, and durable task state. Its Node and React control plane replaces scattered terminal sessions with a governed operating model for multi-agent work.

headline: Hindsight Gives Agents a Longer Memory
lede: Hindsight builds an enduring memory loop around retain, recall, and reflect. With SDKs for Python, Node, and Go and deployment from Docker to Kubernetes, it connects agent workflows to knowledge that survives the conversation.

headline: ModelOpt Compresses AI for Faster Inference
lede: NVIDIA Model Optimizer turns quantization, pruning, distillation, and architecture search into composable model transformations. Its outputs target TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, and SGLang, putting smaller checkpoints and lower latency within reach of production teams.

headline: Univer Builds Office Tools Into Any Product
lede: Univer brings spreadsheets, documents, and presentations to the canvas as modular, embeddable building blocks. A shared Facade API spans browser and Node.js, while plugin and preset modes let teams choose between quick integration and deep control.

headline: TensorFlow Remains Machine Learning’s Giant
lede: TensorFlow still spans the full machine-learning arc, from tensor operations and accelerated training to deployment across devices. Its mature APIs, tutorials, visualization tools, and industrial ecosystem keep the framework embedded in everyday model work.

headline: This Curriculum Teaches AI From the Ground Up
lede: AI Engineering from Scratch lays out 523 lessons across 20 phases, asking learners to derive the math and build the machinery themselves. Python, TypeScript, Rust, and Julia carry the course from neural-network fundamentals to agents and MCP.

headline: OpenBao Locks Down the Credentials Layer
lede: OpenBao stores secrets behind encryption, leases, and tightly scoped access policies. It can issue short-lived database and cloud credentials, renew them, and revoke them automatically—giving operators a community-governed alternative for the keys beneath distributed systems.

headline: Buzz Unifies Teams, Agents, and Git Activity
lede: Buzz makes messages, reviews, workflows, and repository events durable, signed objects in shared rooms. Its Tauri desktop client, Nostr-compatible relay, and scoped agent identities give software teams one auditable workspace for conversation and execution.

headline: VS Code Keeps the Workbench Extensible
lede: Visual Studio Code continues to bind editing, navigation, debugging, source control, and tool integration into a cross-platform workbench. Its extension model and support for containers and Codespaces let the same editor adapt from a student project to a distributed engineering environment.

headline: Reverse Skill Gives Security Agents a Procedure
lede: Reverse Skill routes AI-assisted security work through explicit scope checks, tool verification, and repeatable playbooks. Its frameworks for Frida, IDA, BurpSuite, and related tooling aim to replace guessed commands with evidence-based workflows for reversing and penetration testing.
